The leaf shape is recurved near its end.

recto.definition: the front side of a page in a book or manuscript
examples: The notes are on the recto page.
The text begins on the recto.

recto.definition: referring to the front side of a page
examples: The recto margin is wider than the verso margin.

rip.definition: a sudden tear or break in something flexible
examples: The rip in the sleeve widened after one wash.
He noticed a rip in the paper bag.

rip.definition: to pull apart or tear something quickly
examples: The cat ripped the box open.
Carefully rip the label from the bottle.

rip.definition: a strong current of water moving away from shore
examples: He got caught in a rip and had to be rescued.
Stay calm if you feel a rip current pulling you.

rue.definition: to feel sorry for a past action or choice
examples: She rúed missing the meeting.
I rue the day I ignored the warning.

rook.definition: a chess piece that moves horizontally or vertically any number of squares
examples: He sacrificed a rook to win the game.
The rook protected the back row.

rook.definition: a type of bird that is related to crows and is often seen in groups
examples: A rook landed on the roof.
Rooks were flying over the fields in the morning.

retractor.definition: a device or tool used to pull something back or hold it open
examples: The surgeon used a retractor to move the tissue aside.
A retractor helps keep the wound area visible.

refulgent.definition: shining brightly, especially in a way that looks impressive
examples: The refulgent lights of the stage dazzled the audience.
A refulgent sunset filled the sky.

readies.definition: to make something ready or prepared
examples: We readied the room for the guests.
She readies her equipment before each match.

rattrap.definition: a small trap, often used to catch animals, or a wearable device used to catch something by snapping or catching
examples: The farmer set a rattrap near the barn.
A rattrap can injure an animal quickly.

ruth.definition: the ability or willingness to be cruel or without pity
examples: He showed no ruth toward his opponent.
She acted with mercy instead of ruth.

rigging.definition: ropes, wires, and equipment used to control sails or support a ship’s masts
examples: The crew repaired the rigging before the voyage.
A storm damaged the rigging.

roast.definition: meat cooked in an oven, or an event where someone is teased humorously
examples: We had a chicken roast for dinner.
At the party, they did a roast of the host.

roast.definition: to cook food using dry heat, especially in an oven
examples: They roasted the vegetables until they were soft.
Roast the chicken for about an hour.

roast.definition: to tease someone with humorous criticism
examples: They roasted him at the graduation dinner.
The comedian roasted the politician gently.
She resides in Boston.
How long have you resided here?

record.definition: information stored or written to show what happened or what someone did
examples: The record shows when the payment was made.
I kept a record of my expenses.

record.definition: a set of musical tracks on a disc or tape
examples: I found an old record at the shop.
They listened to a jazz record.

record.definition: to store information or events so they can be kept and checked later
examples: Please record your answers on the form.
The camera recorded the accident.

record.definition: to make a sound or performance using an audio or video device
examples: We recorded the song in one afternoon.
The band will record a new album next month.

refract.definition: to bend or change direction when light passes through a material
examples: Light refracts when it enters water.
The lens is designed to refract the beam.

refractory.definition: refusing to obey or being difficult to control
examples: Some students were refractory and wouldn’t follow rules.
The machine became refractory to the new settings.

refractory.definition: able to withstand high heat without melting or breaking down
examples: Refractory materials line furnaces.
The kiln uses refractory bricks.

rigor.definition: strictness and careful attention to rules, standards, or procedures
examples: The project needed rigor in the testing process.
Her work is known for its rigor.

rule.definition: a statement that tells people what they must or must not do
examples: Read the rules before playing.
The rules of the game were explained clearly.

rule.definition: to decide something officially, especially in law or sports
examples: The judge ruled that the evidence could not be used.
The referee ruled against the team.

rule.definition: to control or have power over a group or country
examples: She ruled the kingdom for ten years.
The dynasty ruled the region for centuries.
My old jacket is ratty, but it still works.
The room looked ratty after the party.

recorder.definition: a small wind instrument with finger holes, often used for learning music
examples: My child plays the recorder at school.
The song is written for recorder and piano.
